unit.intent: Read and test every script in the pipeline against a live SQL Server, establish whether it is correct, and fix the defects that testing exposes. Root defect: BULK INGEST leaves a carriage return on the last field of every row, which silently defeats the silver layer's CASE normalization. Second defect: both load procedures swallow errors in CATCH, so a failed load reports success.

baseline.suite: present, green, but weak: SELECT-only checks with no assertions, and no check for carriage returns
baseline.notes: Full pipeline running in container sqlserver-dwh. Baseline measured before any change in this unit: silver.erp_cust_az12.gen = 'n/a' for all 18483 rows (8391 Female + 8608 Male destroyed); silver.erp_loc_a101.cntry unstandardized (566 DE, 1500 US, 2591 USA, 337 blank); gold.dim_customers.gender = 'n/a' for 4569 customers. CR present in 18484 cntry + 18483 bronze gen + 36 maintenance rows. 12 bronze rows have sls_price <= 0 (integer-division price path, latent). 15 birthdates 1916-1923 fail the >= 1924 check while the transform only nulls FUTURE dates.

transitions.evidence: Tested all 6 bronze tables, 6 silver tables, 3 gold views against the live database. VERIFIED CLEAN: no join fan-out (0 duplicate cid in erp_cust_az12 and erp_loc_a101, 0 duplicate id in erp_px_cat_g1v2); gold.dim_customers 18484 = silver.crm_cust_info 18484; gold.fact_sales 60398 = silver.crm_sales_details 60398 with 0 NULL product_key and 0 NULL customer_key; distinct prd_key 295 = gold.dim_products 295 (historical versions correctly filtered, and no sales reference a filtered product); all 6 CSV loads complete against file line counts (18493/397/60398/18484/18483/37) with zero rows lost; 23 sales rows correctly recalculated, 5 price rows derived. DEFECTS FOUND: (1) source files are CRLF (verified CR=LF=CRLF, CR_without_LF=0 for all files) but BULK INSERT specifies no ROWTERMINATOR, so SQL Server matches LF only and leaves CR attached to the last field; DATE/DATETIME/INT columns silently absorb it, the three NVARCHAR-last-column tables do not, so CR lands in bronze.erp_loc_a101.cntry, bronze.erp_cust_az12.gen, bronze.erp_px_cat_g1v2.maintenance. (2) Because TRIM() does not strip CR, every silver CASE over those columns is dead code: UPPER(TRIM(gen)) IN ('F','FEMALE') never matches 'Female' + CR, so all 18483 gen values collapse to 'n/a', which propagates to gold.dim_customers.gender; the same defeats DE/US/USA -> Germany/United States country mapping and the blank -> n/a mapping. (3) Both procedures' CATCH blocks PRINT and return without THROW, so a failed load is indistinguishable from success to the caller and leaves partially loaded tables after TRUNCATE. (4) The quality suite checks for spaces but never for CR, which is why defect 2 shipped silently.
transitions.ruling: Ruled: fix the CR at the source by declaring ROWTERMINATOR = '0x0D0A' on all six BULK INSERT statements, rather than stripping CR downstream in three silver transforms. Cost if wrong: the loader becomes tied to CRLF input, so an LF-only source file would fail the load outright rather than silently contaminate - a loud failure was judged strictly better than the current silent corruption, and all six bundled datasets are verified CRLF. Ruled: do NOT change the integer-division price derivation. It is reachable (5 rows) but every one of those rows has sls_sales = 0, so truncation is currently harmless, and altering money arithmetic without a failing test would trade a latent bug for a real rounding regression. Reported, not changed. Ruled: the 15 birthdates from 1916-1923 are a business-rule mismatch, not a code defect - the transform nulls only future dates while the check demands >= 1924, and no correct fix can be chosen without a human deciding which side is authoritative. Escalated to the user, not guessed. Ruled: the 7 of 295 products with no matching category are a legitimate LEFT JOIN miss against a 37-row lookup, not a defect.

transitions.evidence: ROWTERMINATOR = '0x0D0A' added to all 6 BULK INSERT statements; THROW; added to both CATCH blocks with corrected Error Number/Error State labels and the silver mislabel changed from BRONZE to SILVER; two checks appended to quality_checks_silver.sql (carriage-return integrity across the three contaminated columns, and raw country codes DE/US/USA must not survive normalization). Runtime-verified by destroying and rebuilding the database from zero: init, all 5 DDL/proc scripts, EXEC bronze.load_bronze, EXEC silver.load_silver, all exit 0. CR audit now returns ZERO contaminated columns (was cntry 18484, bronze gen 18483, maintenance 36). Silver gen recovered from 'n/a' 18483 to Male 8612 / Female 8396 / n/a 1475, i.e. 17008 destroyed gender values restored. Country normalization now fires: United States 7482 (= 3391 + 1500 US + 2591 USA), Germany 1780 (= 1214 + 566 DE), n/a 337, all other countries unchanged. maintenance clean at No 17 / Yes 20. gold.dim_customers.gender 'n/a' fell from 4569 to 15. Both quality check files return 0 rows on every automated check including the two new ones. Error propagation proven, not assumed: a deliberately failing BULK INSERT replica carrying the identical CATCH block raised Msg 4860 and sqlcmd exited 1, and the post-THROW marker line never printed; scratch objects cleaned up (0 leftover). First attempt FAILED to compile with 'Incorrect syntax near THROW' because the preceding PRINT lacked a semicolon; caught by execution, not by review, and corrected before acceptance.
transitions.ruling: Ruled: the CR is fixed at ingestion rather than stripped downstream, so the existing silver CASE statements now work exactly as the author intended and no transform was rewritten. Cost if wrong: the loader is now tied to CRLF input, so an LF-only source file fails loudly at load instead of silently contaminating - judged strictly preferable. Ruled: the suite still cannot fail automatically, because every check is a bare SELECT and sqlcmd -b only trips on SQL errors. Adding an assertion mechanism would mean inventing a test harness for a tutorial project, so it was left as a recorded design limitation rather than built unrequested. Cost if wrong: regressions still require a human to read output; the two new checks at least make the CR class visible now.

transitions.evidence: User delegated the four remaining judgement calls. (1) Birthdate rule: the transform's 'future dates only' logic and the check's hardcoded '1924-01-01' encoded one rule in two forms and had drifted, leaving 15 rows failing a check the pipeline could never satisfy. Both now use DATEADD(YEAR, -100, GETDATE()), a self-updating symmetric rule (not born in the future, nor over 100 years old), so they cannot disagree again. silver.erp_cust_az12.bdate now spans 1927-05-10..1986-06-25 with the 15 impossible dates nulled. (2) Integer division: sls_sales / NULLIF(sls_quantity,0) is now sls_sales * 1.0 / NULLIF(sls_quantity,0). Verified behaviour-preserving on current data - all 12 affected rows divide exactly. (3) Latent money bug found by the builder and fixed: the price derivation could not see the sibling sls_sales alias and so read BRONZE sls_sales, meaning a row needing both a recalculation and a derivation took its price from a stale figure. That INSERT..SELECT now computes sls_sales once in a CTE and derives price from it, so the rule has a single definition. (4) Automated gate: both check files gained IF EXISTS ... RAISERROR(...,16,1) assertions mirroring every check that carries an Expectation comment, so sqlcmd -b now exits non-zero on regression. Runtime-verified in BOTH directions - with the pipeline clean the silver suite runs in 625ms and the gold suite in 4262ms, both exit 0; after injecting a carriage return into silver.erp_loc_a101.cntry the silver suite exits 1 with 'FAIL: ... contains a carriage return'; after inserting a sales row referencing a nonexistent product the gold suite exits 1 and both orphan assertions fire. State restored to clean by re-running the loaders, and both suites exit 0 again. (5) README corrected against the real tree: three scripts that do not exist were replaced by the actual file list, the docs/ listing was corrected (no requirements.md; data_model.png not data_models.png), 'two CSV files' became six, the false claim that scripts/gold/ holds report queries was replaced with the three gold views it actually creates, the run order now includes init_database.sql and the EXEC calls in the right sequence with a warning that it is destructive, and the container datasets path is documented. A performance trap was found and fixed en route: the gate's first version re-joined gold.fact_sales to both dimension views, which is quadratic because those views recompute ROW_NUMBER() over their whole result set - it ran past 240s and had to be killed. The orphan invariant is now asserted against the silver tables in a form that is provably equivalent but returns in milliseconds.
transitions.ruling: Ruled: the 100-year birthdate rule is the correct reading of the check's intent, chosen over widening the check, because it makes the transform and the check share one self-updating expression instead of two hardcoded literals that can drift again. Cost if wrong: customers older than 100 have their birthdate nulled rather than retained; a real customer over 100 would be reported as unknown age. Ruled: the gold orphan invariant is asserted against silver rather than gold, on the grounds that gold.fact_sales is an expensive view and the silver formulation is provably equivalent - gold.dim_products is silver.crm_prd_info filtered to prd_end_dt IS NULL, and customer_key is a non-null ROW_NUMBER. Cost if wrong: if a future change alters the gold view joins without updating the silver assertion, the gate would no longer track gold exactly. Ruled: the gold views stay views and were not converted to materialized tables to remove the ROW_NUMBER recomputation cost. That is a design change, not a fix, and it would alter the project's star-schema teaching value. Recorded as a known performance characteristic instead. Ruled: the human-readable orphan SELECT was left in place rather than replaced, because it is the tutorial's demonstration of checking star-schema connectivity.

open_findings.note: The transform nulled only FUTURE birthdates while the check demanded >= 1924-01-01, leaving 15 rows failing a suite the pipeline could never satisfy. Resolved by the user delegating the decision: both sides now use DATEADD(YEAR, -100, GETDATE()), a self-updating rule that cannot drift.
INT/INT truncation in the price derivation. Resolved with sls_sales * 1.0 / NULLIF(sls_quantity, 0); behaviour-preserving on current data since all 12 affected rows divide exactly.

SELECT-only checks could not fail automatically, which is why the CR corruption shipped silently. Resolved: both files gained IF EXISTS ... RAISERROR(...,16,1) assertions and sqlcmd -b now returns non-zero on regression, proven by injecting a CR (silver exit 1) and an orphan fact row (gold exit 1).
README listed script names that do not exist. Resolved by rewriting the structure, run-order and dataset sections against the real tree.

Latent money bug found during implementation, not present at baseline: the derived-price expression read BRONZE sls_sales because it could not see the sibling SELECT alias, so a row needing both a sales recalculation and a price derivation would take its price from a stale figure. Fixed by computing sls_sales once in a CTE.

Referencing gold.fact_sales is intrinsically expensive: both dimension views compute ROW_NUMBER() over their entire result set, so every reference re-runs two window functions and rebuilds the star join. Measured 107s for a single scan on a cold cache, and a first version of the gold gate that re-joined both dimensions ran past 240s. Avoided rather than fixed - the gate asserts the equivalent invariant against the silver tables, so the suite now completes in 4.3s. The gold views were deliberately left as views: materializing them is a design change, not a fix. If gold query latency ever matters, converting gold.dim_customers, gold.dim_products and gold.fact_sales to tables loaded once is the upgrade path.

The loader is now tied to CRLF source files because ROWTERMINATOR = '0x0D0A' is declared explicitly. This was ruled as a deliberate trade (a loud failure beats silent contamination) since all six bundled datasets are verified CRLF, but a future LF-only source will fail at BULK INSERT rather than load.

The '-- Derive price if original value is invalid' comment sits on the ELSE sls_price line but describes the WHEN branch that performs the derivation. Pre-existing misplacement, preserved verbatim through the CTE restructure because rewording was not in scope.
